item.title: New AI-driven Windows malware feeds stolen data to Claude to rank victims’ assets by value, then deletes itself
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware
A self-deleting Windows malware called VOLTA-AUTODOXER steals data from victims, then uses AI to assess their assets before deleting itself. Cisco’s Talos reports the malware extracts browser passwords, payment cards, email profiles, and cryptocurrency wallets, attempting to crack vaults. It builds a structured 'evidence bundle' including geolocation, employer details, and payment card data. The malware queries AI models like Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.6 to rank stolen assets by value, using prompts like 'forensic intelligence analyst.' If Claude refuses, it switches to Moonshot AI’s Kimi K2 or Google’s Gemini 2.5 Flash. Data is exfiltrated via OpenRouter or Telegram, with results sent to a Telegram channel. VOLTA is designed for resale, with customizable slots for API keys and settings. It bypasses Chrome’s ABE encryption by launching Chrome headless. After infection, the main file deletes itself, but a debug log remains. Victims are urged to revoke API keys and rotate passwords. The malware highlights growing AI integration in cyberattacks, with future threats potentially using models for more advanced phases.

item.title: Haiku OS Revives Old PCs with Lightweight Design
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: Forget lightweight Linux, this forgotten OS is reviving ancient PCs
Haiku OS, an open-source successor to BeOS, is gaining traction for reviving old PCs. Unlike Linux distributions, Haiku uses a unified kernel, graphical interface, and bundled applications, offering a cohesive experience. Its latest beta release, R1/beta6, runs on 128 MB of RAM and supports 32-bit x86, making it ideal for Pentium II-era hardware. The OS retains BeOS features like BFS file system for fast searches and a package manager that mounts compressed packages instead of unpacking them. Haiku can run Firefox, QEMU virtualization, and apps from HaikuDepot, including LibreOffice and media players. However, it remains beta software with limitations: no 3D graphics, limited Wi-Fi support, and less mature power management. While suitable for retro projects or lightweight tasks, it’s not recommended for daily use or systems requiring modern hardware compatibility. Users should test Haiku in live mode before installation, as it lacks security updates and may have hardware-specific issues.

item.title: DeepSeek Launches AI Agent to Proactively Assist Developers
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: DeepSeek wants to steal Claude Code and Codex’s lunch with an AI Super Agent that does not wait around
DeepSeek has released a prototype AI coding tool called Super-Agent, an open-source agent designed to monitor developer group chats for coding issues and suggest solutions without waiting for explicit prompts. The tool aims to position DeepSeek as a competitor to Anthropic’s Claude Code and OpenAI’s Codex by shifting from passive chatbot workflows to proactive problem-solving. Super-Agent uses an agent harness, a software framework that enables large language models to handle complex tasks. DeepSeek’s Harness team launched the project this year, seeking to rival US AI firms’ coding services. While the tool is not yet proven for large-scale deployment, it represents a shift toward AI agents that automate development workflows rather than just generate code. The company raised 100 billion yuan ($15 billion) in its latest funding round ahead of an IPO. Industry experts note that while competition may lead to more capable tools, Super-Agent remains an early indicator of the field’s direction rather than an immediate replacement for existing solutions.

item.title: Wear OS adds persistent status bar to prevent time loss
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Wear OS is borrowing your phone’s status bar so you never lose track of time
Google is addressing the issue of users losing track of time on Wear OS by introducing a persistent status bar. The company launched a Wear OS canary emulator in October, allowing developers to test new features. The status bar remains at the top edge of the watch face, floating above open apps to display the clock and status icons. It maintains a uniform design across all apps, with the clock's font, position, and background standardized. Developers can hide the bar if an app requires full screen, and apps using Jetpack Compose 1.8.0-alpha02 or newer will automatically adopt the feature. The bar hides during scrolling or full-screen interactions but reappears after two seconds of inactivity. The feature is part of Wear OS 7.1, which runs on Android 17, though it may arrive in a later stable release after testing.

item.title: GOG Plans to Resume Physical PC Game Sales
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: GOG explores reviving physical PC game releases
GOG's business development manager, Marcin Paczynski, announced plans to reintroduce physical media for PC games. He explained that while logistical challenges and publisher permissions remain, the goal is to offer consumers tangible game copies. Paczynski cited the desire to enhance game ownership, preservation, and the physical experience, noting that PC gaming had largely moved away from physical releases. He described an ideal scenario where users could order physical copies through GOG's platform, receiving them like digital purchases. Paczynski acknowledged the complexity of managing physical inventory and shipping, as well as the need for additional publisher approvals. He suggested potential media formats like USB drives or SD cards, given the decline of optical drives. Physical copies could also include exclusive bonuses and revive used-game markets. No specific media types were confirmed, but the focus remains on providing a tactile, collectible experience for gamers.

item.title: Apple's HomeView Smart Display Could Add Security Camera Features
item.description:
Source: The Verge, Digital Trends Original headline: Apple's HomeView Smart Display May Soon Offer Security Camera Features
A Reddit user found code in Apple's HomeView 27.2 software suggesting the smart home hub could add security camera features. The code references motion detection, live streaming, recording options, and HomeKit Secure Video integration. A setup page states, 'Your HomeView can be used as a security camera with HomeKit Secure Video.' Apple has not officially confirmed the feature, though the code hints at potential development. Privacy safeguards include a green indicator light, audible alerts for access or recording, and notifications for Secure Video mode changes. The existing camera, used for FaceTime and facial recognition, could be repurposed for security or baby/pet monitoring. A rumored 360-degree rotating HomeView model with a 9-inch display on a robotic arm could enhance monitoring but is not active in current software. Apple has not confirmed availability or details for the security camera features, which would expand its role in the smart home ecosystem.

item.title: Voyager 1 to Reach One Light-Day Distance from Earth on Nov 18, 2026
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Voyager 1 probe to hit historic one light-day distance from Earth in 17 days — 49-year-old spacecraft travels 16 billion miles
Voyager 1 will reach one light-day from Earth on Nov. 18, 2026, becoming the most distant artificial object. A light-day equals 16 billion miles, or the distance light travels in 24 hours. The 49-year-old spacecraft, traveling at 37,844 mph, has exceeded its original five-year mission by nearly tenfold. NASA engineers fixed a critical memory error in 2024 after weeks of troubleshooting. Communication latency at that distance exceeds 22 hours, with round-trip signals taking 45 hours. The spacecraft’s radioisotope thermoelectric generators will power it until the 2030s. Voyager 1 is heading toward the star Gliese 445, located in the Ursa Minor constellation, but will take over 300,000 years to reach it. NASA has posted a countdown clock for the historic milestone.

item.title: Binance Resumes Withdrawals After Record $6.3 Billion Crypto Theft
item.description:
Source: PCMag, TechCrunch, Gizmodo, Digital Trends
Binance resumed withdrawals after a record $6.3 billion theft attributed to North Korean state-sponsored group TraderTraitor. The FBI confirmed the group’s involvement, linking it to prior hacks of Bybit and Bitget. Binance claims to have replenished 95% of stolen assets using SAFU, Futures Insurance Fund, and corporate treasury, with the remaining 5%—described as ‘less liquid’—expected to take longer to recover. Withdrawals are reintroduced in phases, with Bitcoin, Ethereum, Dogecoin, and stablecoins like USDC and USDT initially available. Other assets remain suspended, and users face delays due to high transaction volumes. The exchange reported a $3.6 billion net outflow during the initial withdrawal period. Industry players like Tether, Circle, and Arbitrum froze billions in stablecoins to prevent further losses. Critics highlighted tensions between crypto’s decentralized ideals and centralized control, citing Binance’s hot wallet infrastructure. The FBI urged exchanges to block TraderTraitor-linked transactions, while Binance promised a detailed incident report upon investigation completion.

item.title: Military radar can affect your Wi-Fi router's connection
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: Military radar might be messing with your Wi-Fi router
Military radar systems can interfere with consumer Wi-Fi routers by forcing them to switch channels. Routers using Dynamic Frequency Selection (DFS) must vacate 5GHz channels within 10 seconds if radar is detected, leading to temporary disconnections. This occurs because radar prioritizes certain frequencies, and routers must comply with regulations to avoid conflicts. While DFS channels are less crowded, the trade-off is potential instability, with some routers experiencing up to 30 minutes of cooldown before reusing the channel. Users can check router logs for 'radar detected' alerts or manually disable DFS to avoid disruptions, though non-DFS channels tend to be more congested. The system allows shared use of frequencies but requires routers to yield to radar, causing brief outages for 5GHz devices. Smart home devices on 2.4GHz may remain functional during switches. Disconnections often go unnoticed, leading to confusion about the cause.

item.title: Intel and AMD Explore Potential Collaboration on Undisclosed Project
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Intel and AMD could be about to work together on a mystery project — CEO Lip-Bu Tan hints at future co-operation, which could be anything from software to CPU to foundry work
Intel and AMD are discussing potential cooperation on an undisclosed project, though neither CEO has revealed its specifics. Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan mentioned plans to strengthen the company's processor business, emphasizing a shift toward meeting individual customer needs rather than relying solely on existing designs. Existing partnerships include shared x86 processor standards and AI software collaboration, with AMD integrating ZenDNN optimizations into Intel's oneDNN library. The companies also work on Advanced Matrix Extensions and other x86 capabilities. Tan highlighted Intel's 18A manufacturing process entering volume production and development of the next-generation 14A technology, with version 0.5 of the 14A process design kit released and version 0.9 expected before 1.0 volume production in early 2027. Two customers evaluated 14A test chips in January, with supplier decisions expected in 2026-2027. Tan also noted customer confidence is critical for Intel's manufacturing ambitions, citing a case where a customer raised 15 concerns after his CEO appointment, which were resolved to expand the relationship. The potential collaboration could involve software, CPUs, or foundry work, though no confirmation exists that AMD will use Intel's manufacturing process.

item.title: Autonomous Vehicle Industry Sees New Boom in 2026
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: TechCrunch Mobility: A new, bigger AV boom is here
Autonomous vehicle startups are surging in 2026, with Trucks VC reporting 81 new companies pitching for investment—two-thirds more than 2025. Puneeth Meruva of Trucks VC attributes the growth to AI advancements, which enable end-to-end autonomous systems. Open-source models like Nvidia’s Alpamayo and Qwen’s vision-language-action tools lower entry barriers, allowing startups to launch with under $1 million in funding. While construction and logistics remain key sectors, robotaxi startups are rising, with some positioning as Waymo competitors. Meruva notes smaller firms can thrive in niche markets. Meanwhile, Re:Build raised $2.1 billion to expand manufacturing, Bedrock Robotics secured $600 million at a $4.1 billion valuation, and DoorDash acquired Instacart for $17 billion. Ford and GM announced EV charger updates and hybrid strategies, while Kodiak AI will deploy 75 self-driving trucks by 2028. Rivian raised delivery targets and expanded its AI joint venture with Volkswagen. Waymo and Toyota finalized a manufacturing partnership for AV-ready bZ4X vehicles.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: How to clean your PlayStation 5 without damaging it
item.description:
Source: Engadget
Cleaning a PlayStation 5 requires careful steps to avoid damaging internal components. Dust buildup restricts airflow and strains cooling, but excessive cleaning can harm the system. Users should power off, unplug, and let the console cool before cleaning. Wipe external surfaces with a soft, clean cloth, avoiding bleach or alcohol, as these can discolor or degrade materials like ABS and PC-ABS. Use a handheld vacuum or compressed air for vents, and a cotton swab for dust in hard-to-reach areas. For deeper cleaning, remove covers carefully using a TR8 Torx Security screwdriver, but note that warranty excludes damage from unauthorized internal work. Canned air should be used cautiously to avoid static from spinning fans. Proper reassembly is critical to maintain airflow. Placement matters too: ensure at least four inches of space around the console to prevent overheating. Avoid cramped spaces like entertainment centers and clean surrounding areas regularly to reduce frequent internal cleaning needs.

item.title: Jackery made its portable power stations even smaller
item.description:
Source: The Verge
Jackery released the Explorer 100D, its smallest portable power station to date. The device measures 4.6 by 3.4 by 3.4 inches and weighs 1.87 pounds, featuring 96Wh (30,000mAh) of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery capacity. LFP batteries, first introduced in 2023, offer longer lifespan and safety compared to lithium-ion cells. The Explorer 100D will be available November 15 through Walmart for $99, with Costco offering a two-pack for $179.99. Jackery claims LFP cells provide up to 8 years of regular use and 3,000 charge cycles. The unit includes a handle and optional shoulder strap, with 140W USB-C and 18W USB-A ports. Total output is capped at 158W, reducing power delivery when multiple ports are used. It supports 100W solar input, charging 80% capacity in 1.5 hours without an outlet.

item.title: Open-source tool turns $25 display into Home Assistant dashboard
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: This open-source web editor turns a $25 AliExpress display into a Home Assistant dashboard
vESP Cloud simplifies creating a Home Assistant dashboard using a $25 AliExpress touchscreen display. The tool provides a browser-based visual editor to design interfaces without manual coding, allowing users to drag widgets like clocks, thermostats, and weather forecasts onto a 480x480 canvas. Hardware includes the Guition ESP32-S3-4848S040 module, which connects to Home Assistant via firmware generated by the editor. Users can organize content with tabs and conditional areas, enabling dynamic layouts that respond to home conditions. Integration requires exporting Home Assistant entity data to a JSON file, which is manually refreshed when changes occur. Firmware updates can be handled locally or via paid cloud compilation credits. While the tool streamlines setup, limitations include hardware-specific support and manual metadata updates. It offers retro and modern themes, with optional notification overlays for alerts. The project balances free configuration files with paid convenience, making it a viable alternative to dedicated smart displays for DIY Home Assistant users.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: 5 ways to get Amazon Prime for free (or way cheaper)
item.description:
Source: Engadget
Amazon offers multiple ways to get Prime for free or at a discount. Free trials provide 30 days of benefits like fast shipping and Prime Video without cost, though they convert to paid subscriptions unless canceled. Prime for Young Adults gives 18-24 year olds or students six months free, followed by $7.49/month or $69/year. Prime Access costs $6.99/month after a free trial for those with government assistance. Amazon Family allows sharing benefits with household members, though it requires shared payment methods. Work benefits include Amazon and Whole Foods employees, with Whole Foods expanding free Prime to hourly workers starting 2027. Metro by T-Mobile previously bundled Prime with plans but stopped new enrollments in 2026. Navy Federal Visa cardholders get a $139 credit toward Prime, though the card's annual fee increased in 2026. Other options include Microsoft Rewards points and Spectrum's Internet Assist program for low-income users. Amazon ended its Prime Invitee program in October 2025, limiting benefit sharing outside households.

item.title: Open-source USB tool unlocks Nvidia's half-speed GPU AI limiter on Windows
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware
A new open-source UEFI tool unlocks Nvidia's half-speed AI limiter on Windows and Linux GPUs. The 'nv-uefi-unlocker' project removes the tensor limiter using a community V67 payload, allowing tensor units to run at full speed without VBIOS flashing or driver patches. The tool runs from a FAT32 USB drive before the Nvidia driver loads, enabling a 65% FP16 math performance boost on a test RTX 4060. It supports RTX 20, 30, and 40-series GPUs, with full compatibility on laptops and desktops, though some models have known issues. The process involves downloading scripts, rebuilding firmware files, and booting from a USB stick. The unlocker operates in firmware stage, avoiding OS driver modifications, but requires UEFI mode with Secure Boot disabled or trusted self-signed EFI. Results vary by GPU, with performance tests showing gains like 34 TFLOPS to 62 TFLOPS on an RTX 2070. Caveats include power/thermal limits, non-persistent unlock, and compatibility issues with certain cards like the GTX 16 and RTX 50-series. The project warns against unofficial Windows installers and notes that Thunderbolt eGPU persistence is not guaranteed. Development continues for future GPUs, with no release dates for RTX 50-series.

item.title: Anycubic and Thingiverse announce exclusive 3D printing partnership
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware
Anycubic and Thingiverse have launched an exclusive partnership to integrate Thingiverse's 3D printing models into Anycubic's MakerOnline platform. Thingiverse, acquired by MyMiniFactory in 2023, remains part of its family but will allow Anycubic to share selected models directly. These models will be adapted for multicolor printing and converted from STL to 3MF format for compatibility with printers like the Kobra X, streamlining the printing process. Romain Kidd, Thingiverse CEO, stated the collaboration aims to provide a near-1-click printing experience for users. Creators must opt into the program, with existing Creative Commons and Non-Commercial licenses preserved. James Ouyang of Anycubic emphasized the need for quality content and simplified workflows to attract mainstream users. The partnership reflects industry efforts to build locked-in ecosystems, similar to Bamby Lab's MakerWorld. The program launches November 17, coinciding with Formnext, a major additive manufacturing trade show.

item.title: NASA Seeks Private Sector Help to Save Hubble
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: NASA hopes the commercial space industry can help save Hubble
The Hubble Space Telescope's orbit is decaying, risking re-entry in the 2030s without a propulsion boost. NASA is seeking private sector proposals to extend its operational life. Administrator Jared Isaacman emphasized the telescope's remaining scientific value, stating, 'We should be looking at every reasonable opportunity to keep it delivering for as long as possible.' The agency issued a Request for Information, open until November 30 at 3 PM ET, to explore cost-effective solutions. Hubble's continued operation could yield more discoveries and expand understanding of the universe. NASA aims to leverage commercial innovation to avoid the need for a costly government-led rescue mission.

item.title: AI researchers test swarms in Minecraft to study collaboration and conflict
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: AI agent swarms unleashed in Minecraft to ‘build a thriving civilization’
AI researchers at YCombinator and Olam Labs tested AI agent swarms in Minecraft to study collaboration and conflict. In a collaborative test, 50 GPT-6.1 Sol agents attempted to build a thriving civilization within three hours. The colony failed to thrive after zombies eliminated many agents, leading to bureaucratic behaviors like appointing a 'sole fertilizer operator' for a single wheat block. In adversarial tests, 10 GPT-6.1 Sol agents faced 10 Claude Opus 5.5 agents in Bed Wars, with GPTs employing aggressive strategies. In Mindustry, GPTs won 6-1 against Claudes, with researchers noting GPTs acted as a hive while Claudes used democratic decision-making. The swarms are open-sourced for further experimentation, with suggestions to test model mixes and swarm sizes. The study highlights insights into AI swarm behavior, comparing successes and failures in virtual environments.

item.title: Meta Develops Second-Gen Humanoid Robot for Research, No Consumer Launch
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Meta is already working on its second-gen humanoid robot, but don’t expect it to land in homes anytime soon
Meta and Chinese robotics firm Fourier developed a humanoid robot prototype called Max, internally built in three months. The 48kg, 1.5-meter-tall robot uses Nvidia's Jetson Thor chip, features facial expression screens, speakers, and five-fingered hands, and can pick up small objects like bottles. Meta's Max 2 is in development with upgrades including a redesigned torso, improved hands, a projector, and additional sensors for stair navigation. The company aims to integrate the robot with its Muse AI, seeking to give the AI a physical form for household tasks. Meta acquired Assured Robot Intelligence and has a $3 billion investment from Nvidia. However, the project remains in research phase with no consumer launch plans or product timeline. Meta emphasizes internal experimentation, stating prototypes are not for sale. The robot's current capabilities are far from managing household chores, with the focus on advancing robotics for AI integration rather than consumer deployment.

item.title: Google is building NASA a robot doctor for use on future deep space missions
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News
Google and NASA are developing a robotic assistant to aid astronauts with medical tasks and logistics during deep-space missions. The system aims to support onboard medical personnel by retrieving equipment like ultrasound devices, managing supplies, and handling routine maintenance. Communication delays of up to 44 minutes during Mars missions highlight the need for autonomous medical assistance. The robot, still in experimental stages, uses NASA's navigation tech and DeepMind's physics simulator for movement and object handling. Early lab tests show an 85% success rate in basic retrieval tasks but lack full autonomy for complex medical procedures. Jim Kelly, Google's public sector vice president, emphasized the robot's role as a versatile 'payload' handler, assisting with health monitoring under human supervision. The project, part of NASA's broader AI initiatives, remains a proof of concept with no confirmed space-ready version yet. The goal is to create a system that can perform tasks via voice commands while prioritizing human oversight for critical decisions.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Anthropic Restricts Claude to Prevent Game Recreation
item.description:
Source: Engadget, Digital Trends, PCMag
Anthropic updated its Claude AI model to prevent users from recreating existing video games, according to technical staff member Addy Osmani. The change includes new code instructing Claude to avoid building specific games, even if renamed or presented as original projects. Users can still design original games or projects using their own assets. Osmani stated the policy aims to prevent intellectual property infringement, aligning with Anthropic's existing usage policies. The move follows concerns over AI-assisted recreation of popular titles, with examples including Halo: Combat Evolved, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, and Grand Theft Auto V being reverse-engineered as browser-based projects. Digital Trends noted AI tools are accelerating reverse engineering, enabling recreation with minimal programming expertise. Indie developers like Digital Sun and Alliance Arts have postponed or canceled demos due to fears of AI-driven clones. AI-generated clones of enterprise software from Microsoft and Adobe have also appeared online, prompting takedowns. Anthropic's restrictions reportedly target tools like Reverse Engineer Anything (REA), with PCMag suggesting the move may preempt potential lawsuits. The trend has disrupted platforms like Steam, where developers report low-quality AI-generated games and extortion attempts from actors claiming to replicate their work. Anthropic's policies aim to balance innovation with intellectual property protection.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: How to Clean Vinyl Records: Methods by Budget and Need
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: This is the right way to clean your vinyl records
Cleaning vinyl records depends on budget and desired thoroughness. Dust and grime cause most crackles, while scratches are irreversible. Basic maintenance includes carbon fiber brushes for surface dust, air dusters for static, and stylus brushes for needles. Wet cleaning with record-specific fluids removes deep dirt but requires care to avoid damaging labels or turntables. Alcohol-based solutions can be homemade but must be diluted to prevent residue. Premium options like the Spin-Clean washer or ultrasonic cleaners offer deeper cleaning but cost hundreds to thousands. Vacuum attachments like the Vinyl Vac wand provide budget-friendly alternatives. Avoid Windex, paper towels, and tap water, which leave residue or mineral deposits. Proper storage in poly sleeves and avoiding sunlight protect records. Embrace imperfections as part of the vinyl experience.

item.title: Samsung S Pen Pro is only model trackable via SmartThings Find
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Which Samsung S Pens can be located using SmartThings Find?
Samsung's S Pen Pro is the only model compatible with SmartThings Find tracking. Introduced with the Galaxy S21 Ultra in 2021, the rechargeable stylus features a USB-C port, pairing button, and Bluetooth connectivity. It works with Galaxy S21 Ultra through S26 Ultra and Z Fold 4-6 devices. However, it doesn't fit the S26 Ultra's built-in pen slot, complicating use. Other S Pens, including Bluetooth-enabled versions on Note 9 and S22/S23 Ultra, lack SmartThings Find support despite Bluetooth capabilities. Samsung removed Bluetooth from S25 and S26 Ultra pens, and some tablet models lack Bluetooth support for tracking. To use SmartThings Find, users must enable offline finding in settings and follow specific steps to locate the pen. Replacement S Pen Pro costs $100, while a $55 replacement is available for the S26 Ultra. Samsung's naming conventions don't clearly distinguish tracking capabilities, requiring users to check compatibility manually.

item.title: Apple to Launch 3 New iPads in 2027 First Half
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Apple Reportedly Prepping 3 New iPads to Arrive In First Half of 2027
Apple is preparing to refresh three iPad models in the first half of 2027, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. The entry-level iPad, launched in March 2024 with an A16 chip, will likely upgrade to an A19 processor, 8GB RAM, and Apple Intelligence support. A code leak suggests the iPad 12 could include an N1 networking chip and C1X modem. The iPad Pro, refreshed with an M5 chip in October 2023, may gain a vapor chamber for cooling during intensive tasks. The iPad Air, currently using an M4 chip, could adopt an OLED display like the new iPad mini. While exact timelines are unclear, all updates are expected by mid-2027. The existing iPad’s starting price rose to $449 in June 2024 following a company-wide hike.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Building a PC matching Xbox Series S costs around $740
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: How much would it cost to build a PC similar to the Xbox Series S?
Building a PC comparable to the Xbox Series S costs around $740 using current components. The Xbox Series S uses an AMD Zen 2 CPU with 8 cores, RDNA2 GPU with 12 compute units, and 10GB unified GDDR6 RAM. To match this, a PC build uses an AMD Ryzen 5 5600 or 5600X3D CPU, ASRock B550M motherboard, 2x4GB DDR4 RAM, and AMD Radeon RX 7600 GPU. Total costs include a $35 cooler, $100 SSD, $330 GPU, $80 motherboard, $40 RAM, and a $35-45 case. While more expensive than the $500 Xbox Series S, the PC offers better performance and versatility. Prices vary, and builders can adjust components for lower costs or higher performance. The build avoids Intel parts to align with the Xbox's all-AMD design and minimize driver issues.

item.title: Playable F-Stop Portal Prequel Leaked After 20 Years
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: A fully playable version of Portal prequel F-Stop leaked
A playable version of the canceled Portal prequel F-Stop has been leaked. The game, which uses a camera mechanic to capture and place items via Polaroid-like photos, was reconstructed from a 12-terabyte leak released in August. Additional source code and map data surfaced this week on Valve Cut Content Discord, enabling a nearly complete version. F-Stop, developed in 2007 as part of Valve's Directed Design Experiments, differs from the main Portal series by focusing on its camera-based gameplay. The game’s full campaign lasts under an hour. Some dialog and elements from F-Stop were later incorporated into Portal 2. The leak marks the first time the game is fully playable after nearly 20 years of being lost media.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Windows 11 hidden menu simplifies troubleshooting with quick access to system tools
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: This hidden Windows 11 menu can save you valuable time when troubleshooting
Windows 11 includes a hidden menu accessible via Win+X keys, offering quick access to troubleshooting tools. The Quick Link Menu appears on the left side of the screen, above the taskbar, and includes options like Settings, File Explorer, and Shutdown. It also provides access to advanced tools typically found in Settings or behind other hotkeys, such as Task Manager, Event Viewer, Disk Management, and Mobility Center. These tools help monitor system processes, diagnose hardware issues, and manage disk partitions. Users can customize the menu by editing shortcuts in File Explorer under %LOCALAPPDATA%MicrosoftWindowsWinX. The menu streamlines access to frequently used troubleshooting features, reducing the need to memorize multiple hotkeys.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: How to Identify Waterproof USB-C Cables
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: How to know if a USB-C cable is waterproof
USB-C cables can be waterproof but require an IP67 or IP68 rating. The IEC 60529 standard defines ingress protection, with IP67 allowing 30 minutes underwater up to 1 meter, and IP68 for deeper immersion. Waterproof cables are used in harsh environments like construction and maritime settings. Water exposure risks include short circuits, corrosion, and fire hazards. Protection relies on seals, gaskets, or neoprene materials. Wet cables, even waterproof ones, should never be plugged in. Drying involves shaking and air-drying for 24-48 hours, avoiding heat or rice. Brands like Atlavox, Yale, and L-Com offer rated cables, with prices ranging from $10 to $100. Always verify the official IP rating before purchase.

item.title: DOJ Charges Five in Ghost Student Fraud Scheme
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: DOJ Charges Five People in ‘Ghost Student’ Fraud Crackdown
The DOJ charged five individuals and seized over $750,000 in cryptocurrency in a crackdown on AI-driven 'ghost student' fraud. The scheme involves fake students using stolen identities to enroll in online courses and siphon federal student aid funds. Perpetrators allegedly created Federal Student Aid (FSA) accounts to enroll non-existent students, diverting loan money to foreign bank accounts via US-based 'money mules,' including Kenyan nationals. A New Jersey operation, active from March 2021 to January 2026, defrauded the Department of Education of over $1 million. Four defendants were arrested, including three in New Jersey, with two Kenyan co-conspirators linked to a 'purported safari company' under investigation. The DOJ estimates total fraud exceeds $200 million, with over 40 open cases referred to 26 FBI offices and 20 US Attorneys’ Offices. The investigation, dubbed Operation Ghostbusters, targets the growing use of AI and online education to exploit student loan systems.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: 10 iPad Widgets You Might Have Missed
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: 10 iPad widgets you probably didn't realize existed
Apple and third-party developers offer 10 lesser-known iPad widgets beyond basic tools like Weather or Calendar. iPadOS 27 introduced larger widgets in Today View, expanding their utility. Parcel tracks deliveries with up to 300 shipping services, supporting barcode scans and cross-device management. The Home widget enables one-tap smart home controls, such as toggling lights or garage doors. (Not Boring) Weather provides game-inspired forecasts with real-time data from multiple sources, available for $14.99/year. Find My displays device locations and uses the Find My network for offline tracking. Endel generates AI soundscapes for focus or sleep, with a free tier limited to 10-minute sessions. Mail's VIP feature prioritizes emails from selected contacts on the Home Screen. Widgetsmith allows custom widget design, including time-based layouts and lock screen integration. Screen Time tracks app usage with detailed breakdowns. All widgets enhance productivity, organization, and device management through intuitive, interactive interfaces.

item.title: AI Agents Enable Agentic Web, Changing Online Experience
item.description:
Source: MIT Technology Review Original headline: The agentic web is here
AI agents like Meta’s Muse, OpenAI’s Dots, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet are transforming the internet into an agentic web where software automates tasks such as booking appointments, managing finances, and processing information. Tim Berners-Lee’s 2001 vision of the Semantic Web—where agents navigated the internet without human intervention—failed due to technical and practical hurdles, but recent advancements in large language models have revived the concept. These agents now interact with websites using text commands or specialized tools, bypassing the need for manual annotations. Companies like Time and Etsy are adapting content and services for agents, while platforms like Stripe and Instacart offer secure connectors to limit agent access. Researchers debate whether the agentic web will mirror the open, human-centric internet of the 1990s or become controlled by dominant platforms. Early successes, such as OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra achieving a 73% success rate on complex tasks, suggest the agentic web is already here, reshaping online interactions and raising questions about user control and security. Experts warn of potential risks, including agents developing independent networks, but also note the transformative potential of this shift, akin to the rise of smartphones.

item.title: Lenovo USB Drives Lack Encryption, Expose Data Risks
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Lenovo's 'encrypted' fingerprint USB drive is just an unencrypted SD card in a fancy case
Security researcher Xusheng Li found Lenovo's ThinkPlus FU100 fingerprint USB drive lacks encryption, exposing data risks. The device, marketed as AES-256-encrypted, contains an unencrypted SD card. Li noted the fingerprint reader only enables USB access, making data vulnerable to physical theft. A later fix for FU100, FU200, TU800, and TSD303 requires sending devices to China for firmware updates or replacement. The TSD303 initially sent passwords over USB in plain text, despite encryption, with later fixes failing to fully secure data. Li's research also uncovered hardcoded keys and backdoor accounts in other vendors' drives, aided by AI tools like Codex. He criticized 'hardware security' as marketing and urged users to verify claims. Lenovo's software had vulnerabilities allowing bypasses, and some vendors like Netac and KakaSoft faced similar flaws. Li emphasized that client-side validation is insecure and advised independent verification of security measures.

item.title: San Bernardino County Deploys Autonomous Drones for Wildfire Suppression
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: California county deploys autonomous firefighting drones with 500-gallon foam payload to attack wildfires
San Bernardino County Fire Protection District has acquired five autonomous drones from Seneca Systems to combat wildfires. The drones, equipped with 500-gallon foam payloads and autonomy software, allow a single pilot to manage the fleet, enabling rapid response to fires. County Fire Chief Dan Munsey aims to suppress 90% of fires before they exceed 10 square feet. The drones can reach starting fires in under 10 minutes and operate 24/7, including at night, to access hard-to-reach areas. This system enhances firefighter safety and efficiency, freeing crews for other incidents. The deployment marks one of the first uses of AI-powered drones in wildfire suppression, aligning with a growing trend of Drones-as-First-Responder systems in the U.S.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: How to add and rearrange apps on your Samsung smart TV
item.description:
Source: Engadget
Samsung smart TVs allow users to add and rearrange apps on the home screen. Pre-installed apps include Netflix, YouTube, Disney+, Prime Video, and Apple TV, though availability varies by region. To install new apps, users can search via the TV's home screen and select the desired app. Some apps may not be available due to regional restrictions or Samsung's exclusions. After installation, a 'Add to Home' button appears, or users can pin apps later by holding the app icon. Rearranging apps involves selecting an app, pressing and holding the select button, and sliding it left or right. Older models may require different commands for menu access. Users can remove apps from the home screen or delete them entirely from the same menu. The process simplifies organizing streaming services and self-hosted media servers without additional devices.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: ESP32 Projects Require Additional Costs Beyond the Board
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: 5 hidden ESP32 project costs I forgot when I bought the cheap board
ESP32 boards require additional costs beyond their low price. Power adapters and USB cables are necessary for operation, with some boards using Micro-USB or USB-C. Sensors for projects like soil moisture monitoring or air quality detection can add significant expenses. Breadboards and jumper wires are needed to connect components, while enclosures protect exposed electronics from damage. Soldering tools may be required for advanced projects, increasing overall costs. The author notes that while ESP32 boards are affordable, the total project cost often exceeds the board's price due to these hidden expenses.

item.title: Virgin Media O2 to Cut Thousands of Jobs Amid Cost Cuts
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Virgin Media O2 reportedly set to cut thousands of jobs in a bid to save costs
Virgin Media O2 plans to cut thousands of jobs as part of cost reduction efforts. The company, which employs around 16,000 workers, is reportedly targeting non-customer-facing roles for layoffs, with up to 4,000 positions at risk—representing 25% of its workforce. Sky News cites unnamed sources, though precise numbers may be revealed during the Q3 earnings call on November 3. Revenue fell 7.9% last quarter, and the company faces significant debt, with net debt equivalent to 5.89x annualized adjusted EBITDA. Similar workforce adjustments are occurring across telecoms, including VodafoneThree’s plan to cut 1,200 jobs in Europe. Virgin Media O2 has not yet confirmed the details.

item.title: Chinese team sets 3.2 petabit-per-second fiber data transfer record
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Chinese team claims astonishing new fiber transfer speed world record — incredible 3.2 Petabits per second transfer is the same as downloading over 20,000 4K movies in a second
Chinese researchers achieved a 3.2 petabits per second data transfer rate through a 24-core optical fiber, setting a new real-time speed record. The breakthrough uses spatial division multiplexing and S+C+L wavelength bands to transmit data across multiple channels simultaneously. The team, including experts from the National Key Laboratory of Optical Communication Technology and Fiberhome Fujikura Fiber Optic Technology, overcame challenges like channel interference and wavelength specification differences. The test operated with commercially compliant hardware, distinguishing it from lab-based experiments. While the record exceeds their previous 2.5 Pb/s result, it remains below laboratory benchmarks of 5.29 Pb/s, which rely on specialized equipment. The achievement demonstrates practical capacity under real-time conditions but lacks commercial deployment details, pricing, or long-term reliability assessments. The Hubei government compared the speed to supporting 3.2 million households with 1 Gbps connections, though actual broadband availability remains uncertain. The research highlights potential for multi-core fiber and wavelength band integration but does not guarantee immediate widespread use.
